title: Dakar 2027: Portugal - Morocco
status: Route as published by ASO on 2026-10-30 (press release as reported by RACER, 2026-10-30): start Jan 9 at the Algarve Stadium (Loule-Faro), prologue then stage 1, transfer to a Mediterranean port and an overnight crossing to Nador, landing Jan 11, first Moroccan bivouac Bouarfa, then south along the Atlas via Zagora to Agadir (rest day), the far south (Smara, almost to Dakhla), back north to the finish in Marrakech on Jan 23; 4,341 km of specials. Stage-by-stage detail (specials, totals, bivouacs, the refuge) is from one secondary write-up of that route (video of 2026-10-31); dakar.com's route page, when read for this, still showed another event's table, so nothing is taken from it. Everything below the day level (the roads and tracks each stage follows) is NOT published yet: it is authored here, see 'note' and each leg's own note.
sources: https://racer.com/2026/10/30/dakar-rally-set-for-portugal-to-morocco-route-in-2027 (ASO's announcement of 2026-10-30: dates, Algarve Stadium, overnight crossing to Nador, Bouarfa, Zagora, Agadir rest day, Smara, almost Dakhla, 4,341 km of specials, 350-500 km stages)

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pMfhg0aBft4 (Dakar 2027 route explained, 2026-10-31: the stage-by-stage table of this file, 29 km prologue in a cork forest, the refuge, the 1,035 km day, 'the port and the ships are not named yet')
unconfirmed: The Spanish port. ASO has named none; Almeria (Almeria-Nador, the shortest sea crossing from the Spanish coast nearest the Algarve road that has a regular ferry line) is the working assumption. Beni Ensar (Nador) is the landing: it is the port of Nador.

Each stage's real itinerary and every liaison: only the start and finish towns are published. The stages here follow plausible pistes and roads between those towns, lengths tuned to the published special km.

The official total km of a day includes liaisons ASO has not described; the liaisons here take the road between the bivouacs and the stage start and finish, so a day's total is not the official one (see each leg's 'officialKm' and the table in the docs).
The 590 km of the stage-1 day is read as the transfer to the port (Loule-Almeria is 605 km by road); the 300 km 'total' of stage 1 as its own liaisons plus the special.
T2 (Nador - Bouarfa) has no official km; the road is about 413 km.
The marathon refuge's place near the Dakhla lagoon (stage 8 ends there, stage 9 starts there).
note: Leg types: special = timed stage (BeamNG rallyStage), transfer = timed liaison (rallyRoadSection), ferry = teleport leg (no driving: core.lua crossFerry takes the player from the departure port to the landing, the next day's loop starts there), rest = no event. Each day (see 'days') is a loop of its own in the mission list: its liaison to the start, the special, and the liaison on to the next bivouac, the day starting where the day before ended. Leg 'router': osrm = along roads (OSRM), piste = along Overture's tracks, straight lines where it has none (tools/roadnet.py; the leg's geometry file says how many metres are off the network), straight = the via points as they are. specialKm is the published length of a special; the built one is in the geometry file (tools/fetch_route.py --plan lists both).

legs.title: Prologue, cork forest
legs.note: Authored: a 29 km stretch of the cork-oak hills north of Loule (the roads between Sao Bras de Alportel and Salir); ASO says only 'a prologue in a cork forest'. The liaisons are short (19 and 26 km) against the 100 km of the official total of 129 km; the prologue ends heading away from Loule, so the liaison back turns round at the finish.

legs.title: Prologue finish to the Algarve Stadium
Stage 1, Loule/Faro
legs.note: Authored: the Caldeirao hills and the Guadiana valley between Alte and Alcoutim (100 km, as published); ASO says only 'Loule/Faro'. The 300 km 'total' is not matched: the liaison to the port (T1) starts at the stage's finish.

legs.title: Algarve to the port of Almeria
legs.note: The published 590 km is read as this transfer, from the end of stage 1 near Alcoutim to the port of Almeria (built 582 km by road); Loule - Almeria itself is 605 km. The port is assumed: ASO has not named it.

legs.title: Almeria to Nador, overnight
legs.crossing: overnight, boarding on the night of Jan 10, landing on Jan 11 (ASO: the crossing is overnight; the port of embarkation is not named)
legs.note: No driving: the loop of the day ends at the port; the next day's loop (T2) starts at Beni Ensar.

legs.title: Nador to Bouarfa
legs.note: No official km. Nador (Beni Ensar port) to Bouarfa by road, built 414 km.

legs.title: Stage 2, Rekkam plateau
legs.note: Authored: ASO has published only the start and finish towns of this stage and its km. The route follows the tracks Overture Maps has, and straight lines across the dunes and the hamada where it has none (offNetworkM in its geometry file) between waypoints chosen near them and is tuned to the published special km; the liaisons are the roads between the bivouacs and the stage ends, so the day's total km is not the official one (official liaison km of the day: 100).
